family.text: Your brother takes {qty} GPUs to render a wedding video in 8K. It was filmed on a flip phone.
Your dad installs {qty} GPUs for Microsoft Flight Simulator. He flies exclusively over his own driveway.
Your kid takes {qty} NPUs for a smart toaster. It now refuses to make anything but artisan sourdough.
Your cousin takes {qty} NPUs to make a smart mirror. Its only inference is 'go back to bed.'
Your sister takes {qty} TPUs to run a TensorFlow plant classifier. It has diagnosed every houseplant as a salad.
Your aunt takes {qty} TPUs for a recipe model. It keeps suggesting that she preheat the tensor.
Your mom takes {qty} stacks of HBM for her old laptop. It still spends four minutes booting into a coupon toolbar.
Your cousin borrows {qty} HBM stacks for a robot vacuum. It remembers every crumb but keeps eating socks.
Your uncle takes {qty} H100s to predict hockey. The model says the Leafs will win the Cup. Nobody trusts the validation set.
Your dad puts {qty} H100s in a home assistant. It has the power budget of an office and the manners of a teenager.
Your niece takes {qty} Cardputer Zeros to lora chat friends at camp. Everyone now communicates in shell commands.
Your daughter takes {qty} Cardputer Zeros for a scavenger hunt. The first clue is finding the underscore key.
Your cousin takes {qty} CPUs for a home server. Its busiest thread is a cron job that orders more CPUs.
Your aunt swipes {qty} CPUs for a bookkeeping rig. She still does the actual math on an adding machine.
Your nephew swipes {qty} VRAM modules to load ultra textures. He plays on a 720p monitor.
Your daughter takes {qty} VRAM modules to render a virtual hamster. Its individual whiskers have individual whiskers.
Your son takes {qty} chiplets for a Lego build. He calls the bricks an advanced packaging substrate.
Your dad pockets {qty} chiplets for a desktop upgrade. He asks which end of the USB cable takes bare silicon.
Your dad takes {qty} B200s to run DeepSeek. He says he'll give them back after downloading the internet.
Your cousin puts {qty} B200s on a model leaderboard. The first thing he benchmarks is his new electrical panel.
Your cousin takes {qty} AI ASICs to save power on inference. He leaves his rack fans at full blast for ambience.
Your dad borrows {qty} AI ASICs for a security camera. They detect packages with exceptional efficiency and ignore the porch thief.
Your brother uses {qty} units of neural fabric to fix his gaming lag. He's still playing on hotel Wi-Fi.
Your partner takes {qty} neural fabric units to wire the house. The thermostat now negotiates with the fridge at line rate.
Your sister uses {qty} optical transceivers to link her streaming PC. Her ISP still caps uploads at ten megabits.
Your cousin takes {qty} optical transceivers to wire his apartment. They cost more than the security deposit he drilled through.
Your uncle borrows {qty} storage pods to archive his VHS tapes. He saves every frame as an uncompressed TIFF.
Your grandma fills {qty} storage pods with genealogy scans. She keeps the only copy of the index in a shoebox.
Your teenager feeds {qty} Reddit datasets to a chatbot. Every answer starts with 'Actually, you're wrong.'
Your aunt nabs {qty} Reddit datasets for a recipe bot. Every recipe starts with an argument about cast iron.
Your dad gives {qty} AI tokens to his bowling league. It turns out the vending machine still takes quarters.
Your nephew takes {qty} AI tokens to teach a bot about finance. It learns to announce a token presale.
Your mom takes {qty} silicon wafers for serving plates. The cheese course now requires cleanroom gloves.
Your brother takes {qty} lots of fab materials for garage chipmaking. The cleanroom is also where he sands drywall.
Your cousin grabs {qty} proprietary weight bundles to run a local assistant. He names it Offline and gives it his cloud password.
Your brother tries to merge {qty} model checkpoints. The result speaks fluent YAML and refuses to answer questions.
Your aunt buys party supplies with {qty} AGI futures. The balloons are contingent on a breakthrough in reasoning.
Your brother trades {qty} AGI futures for a promise to automate laundry. The dryer is still waiting for general intelligence.

up.title: AI GOLD RUSH!
up.text: Every corporation on Earth just announced plans to achieve AGI by Friday. Investors are buying anything with a circuit board.

up.title: SILICON FEVER!
up.text: AI companies have begun buying each other's supplies in an infinite bidding war. Economists describe the situation as "deeply stupid, but profitable."

up.title: FOMO PANDEMIC!
up.text: A viral post claims AI will replace humanity by Tuesday. Every tech commodity is skyrocketing. Humanity remains suspiciously unconcerned.

up.title: RAM ALTMAN SPEAKS!
up.text: After announcing that "compute is the new oxygen," global tech markets explode. Breathing is now a subscription service.

up.title: THE GREAT AI ARMS RACE!
up.text: Governments worldwide are stockpiling everything with a processor. Even smart toasters are trading at record highs.

up.title: MONEY PRINTER GO BRRR!
up.text: Central banks announce unlimited funding for AI development. Commodity prices soar as financial responsibility becomes obsolete.

up.title: SKYNET IPO ANNOUNCED!
up.text: A mysterious AI announces plans to go public. Investors immediately mortgage their children to buy anything remotely technological.

up.title: CORPORATE PANIC BUYING!
up.text: Every major tech CEO claims to be "six months from AGI." Supply prices explode. Nobody asks why they've been saying that for six years.

down.title: AI BUBBLE BURSTS!
down.text: Investors discover that adding "AI-powered" to a product doesn't actually make it useful. Global tech markets implode.

down.title: THE GREAT UNPLUGGING!
down.text: A worldwide AI outage forces people to think for themselves. Productivity plummets, and every technology commodity crashes.

down.title: RAM ALTMAN SNEEZES!
down.text: Wall Street interprets it as a warning about AI profitability. Every commodity crashes before he can say "excuse me."

down.title: AGI ACHIEVED!
down.text: Scientists unveil the world's first superintelligence. Its first recommendation? Stop wasting money on AI. Markets collapse.

down.title: THE BIG SHORT CIRCUIT!
down.text: A leaked report reveals that 94% of AI startups are just ChatGPT wrappers. Investors flee faster than unpaid interns.

down.title: GLOBAL TECH MELTDOWN!
down.text: Every major AI company announces record losses. Executives reassure shareholders that bankruptcy is merely "negative growth."

down.title: OPEN SOURCE APOCALYPSE!
down.text: A teenager releases a free AI model that outperforms billion-dollar systems. Every tech commodity crashes. Venture capitalists begin crying.

down.title: THE GREAT AI RECALL!
down.text: Researchers discover that most AI systems have been confidently making things up. Markets collapse as executives realize they've been doing the same thing.

news.headline: A new image model needs six consumer GPUs to draw one cat. It still has seven paws.
Crypto miners discover electricity bills. Their GPUs arrive on eBay marked 'lightly screamed at.'
Investors declare consumer GPUs the new gold. Gold investors ask where to plug in the power cable.
A new GPU generation lands. Yesterday's flagship now qualifies for a museum discount.
Every indie AI lab wants a local training rig. The gaming aisle is now a data centre waiting room.
Laptop makers mandate NPUs. A spokesperson promises to find out what they do next quarter.
An NPU takes three minutes to summarize Hello World. The summary is 'Hello.'
Privacy campaigners push for offline assistants. NPUs finally have a job their owners asked for.
An OS update sends AI features back to the cloud. Laptop NPUs return to decorative silicon duty.
Corporate IT mandates NPU laptops. The approved AI workload is still a 14-year-old Excel macro.
A cloud lab reserves an entire TPU pod for matrix math. The spreadsheet team asks if it can borrow a row.
A model compiler finally runs on ordinary GPUs. TPU reservations vanish faster than the migration guide.
A new TensorFlow benchmark loves TPUs. The benchmark authors also happen to rent TPUs.
A cloud region dumps old TPUs after a pod upgrade. Each pallet comes with a mandatory compiler tutorial.
A giant transformer trains efficiently on TPUs. Suddenly every lab calls its matrix multiply 'strategic.'
An AI lab bids for all the HBM on Earth. Analysts suspect the next model is God with a context window.
A new model needs 4 TB of HBM to tell the time. Its answer is 'approximately.'
Memory makers ramp HBM output. Scarcity enthusiasts request a recall on the good news.
Next-gen accelerators stack enough HBM to bankrupt a small country. The spec sheet calls it a footnote.
A memory-saving breakthrough slashes HBM demand. Hardware executives demand a recount.
Export controls make H100s harder to get than concert tickets. At least the scalpers know the form.
A newer accelerator ships. H100 owners start putting 'collector grade' in their listings.
A production model still needs H100s. Its biggest customer is the team writing its own replacement.
A data centre expansion snaps up the last H100s. The building permit lists 'autocomplete' as the occupant.
New H100 rental capacity sends rates tumbling. Owning one now comes with complimentary buyer's remorse.
A pocket Linux terminal goes viral. Cardputer Zero buyers apparently already own six keyboards.
A fresh Cardputer Zero batch lands. Resellers pivot from 'rare dev kit' to 'shipping included.'
A tiny terminal contest puts Cardputer Zero in every project photo. The keyboards look enormous beside the trophies.
A rival handheld ships with a bigger display. Cardputer Zero owners can now read the resale prices.
A maker ports a retro game to Cardputer Zero. Thousands buy one to avoid finishing their own ports.
Scientists rediscover that computers contain CPUs. The CPUs ask why this wasn't in the press release.
An AI lab replaces 400 servers with a GPU cluster. The CPUs get reassigned to expense reports.
Enterprise inference moves back to CPUs. Vendors swear it was on the roadmap all along.
A new AI-branded CPU benchmarks like the old one. The sticker, however, is 40% faster.
A chiplet shortage slows server CPU shipments. Buyers discover 'two sockets' means two waiting lists.
Local image generation eats VRAM. GPU owners discover their eight gigabytes are actually an entry fee.
A GDDR supply glut hits VRAM module prices. The board vendors still call sixteen gigs 'premium.'
A texture pack demands another 12 GB of VRAM. The game's original box art had three colours.
Quantized image models squeeze into less VRAM. Memory sales forecasts now fit on one Post-it.
A graphics card vendor doubles its VRAM spec after reviews. It calls the original model a limited edition.
Chiplet packaging capacity sells out. The chip is modular, but apparently the waiting list isn't.
A new die-to-die standard makes chiplets interchangeable. Proprietary connector vendors ask for a recount.
A server CPU adds more compute chiplets. Marketing calls the empty space between them 'AI adjacency.'
An advanced packaging yield breakthrough floods the market with chiplets. The defect bins feel neglected.
A foundry splits a massive die into chiplets. Somehow the invoice is still one indivisible number.
An AI lab orders enough B200s to heat a Canadian city. City council asks if winter support is included.
Cooling delays stall B200 installations. Data centre operators consider building the next rack in a rink.
A reasoning model sends B200 demand soaring. NVIDIA executives start comparing yacht benchmarks.
A next-gen roadmap leaks. B200 owners experience buyer's remorse before delivery.
One hyperscaler reserves the next B200 shipment. Independent researchers begin bargaining with destiny.
A giant inference service orders custom AI ASICs. The chip's only other mode is 'off.'
A model update needs an operation the AI ASIC can't run. Its resale listing calls that 'focus.'
Power budgets tighten. Efficient inference ASICs get the contracts, and GPUs get an intervention.
A vendor cancels its AI accelerator platform. Pallets of ASICs come with a lifetime supply of old drivers.
A custom inference ASIC beats GPUs on tokens per watt. The demo kindly declines to discuss training.
A training cluster hits a network bottleneck. Its GPUs spent the week waiting for packets.
An interconnect firmware update turns a neural fabric into an expensive LAN party.
A hyperscaler rebuilds its AI fabric. Somehow the cable ties account for half the budget.
An open standard challenges proprietary neural fabrics. Vendors file a bug against competition.
A distributed training breakthrough needs twice the fabric bandwidth. Network engineers request vacation.
Data centres roll out 800G optics. Engineers start measuring lead times in generations of fiber.
Co-packaged optics threaten pluggable transceivers. Vendors rebrand the old modules as 'serviceable.'
A supplier runs short of laser diodes. The optical-transceiver roadmap is temporarily in the dark.
A standards update lets cheap optics pass validation. The vendor-approved modules demand a retest.
A city-scale AI cluster orders long-reach transceivers. Its procurement team can see the quote from orbit.
A training set ingests 47 million lunch photos. Petabyte storage orders include a side of fries.
A cloud provider finds three warehouses of unused storage pods. Its inventory system ran out of disk space.
Researchers refuse to delete old checkpoints. Each petabyte pod is marked 'final-final-v2.'
Dataset deduplication frees enough rack storage to cancel a purchase order. One cat video survives.
A lab buys petabyte pods to retain every AI chat. Its compliance team describes this as forgetting responsibly.
Reddit tightens API access. The price of a Star Wars argument is now a licensing negotiation.
A Reddit corpus audit finds confidently wrong advice. The auditors get downvoted for citing sources.
Labs bid for fresh Reddit conversations. Volunteer moderators demand hazard pay.
Synthetic training data catches on. Human arguments temporarily lose market share.
A Reddit-trained model sets a benchmark for passive aggression. Enterprise clients describe it as candid.
An AI coin promises to replace money, banking, and arithmetic. The token supply is 'ask the bot.'
An AI token founder vanishes with the treasury. The farewell note thanks everyone for the prompt.
An influencer guarantees his AI coin will reach the moon. Astronomers decline to confirm the listing.
Regulators ask what an AI token actually does. The developers schedule six more months of discovery.
An AI trading bot discovers it has spent three weeks buying its own tokens. It awards itself market maker of the year.
An earthquake disrupts wafer output. Chip buyers briefly consider learning patience.
A foundry posts record yields. Fab-material traders are furious that the process works.
Lithography expansion sends demand for high-purity fab materials soaring. Even the dust needs a reservation.
A new wafer plant opens ahead of schedule. Speculators ask whether that's even allowed.
Export restrictions hit chipmaking materials. Purified silicon suddenly gets its own foreign policy desk.
A private fine-tune beats the big labs on code. The price of its weights now includes a startup valuation.
An open-weights model beats a proprietary rival. The rival announces a new benchmark.
An AI licensing deal locks up a popular checkpoint. The tensors are now sold by people in suits.
A major model vendor publishes its weights. The old download link still asks for a sales call.
A local inference runtime makes a prized checkpoint run offline. Its former API team discovers withholding.
A lab declares AGI on its own benchmark. Futures spike before anyone opens the benchmark spreadsheet.
An AGI demo turns out to be a room full of contractors. The futures desk calls it human-in-the-loop.
A prediction market moves its AGI date forward. The people making the bets also define 'general.'
A benchmark audit finds the answers in the training set. AGI futures are suddenly graded on a curve.
An AI lab adds 'AGI' to a funding slide. The futures market has seen enough evidence.
